name: Anthropocene and its Discontents
description: The course will introduce students to the “Anthropocene”, its competing definitions, different theories about the relationship between humans and ‘nature’, debates around climate change and the environment, relationships between humans and other species, as well as the role of technology in reshaping life on earth. It will look at other formulations such as Capitalocene, Plantationocene and Chthulucene to study issues of social, epistemic and ecological justice. It will draw upon readings in sociology, social anthropology, history, science and technology studies, philosophy and literature on the Anthropocene.
